evidence: New subparser added at bridge.py:120: `suggest_mapping = commands.add_parser("suggest-mapping", ...)` — not reflected in the metavar literal
help/bridge.txt lines 2/11 show the usage metavar WITHOUT suggest-mapping, but lines 24-25 list `suggest-mapping` in the commands block — the two lists disagree
The same hardcoded metavar is pinned at tests/unit/test_cli_parser_contract.py:107, so the literal is a hand-maintained string that drifts when subparsers change
advisory.finding: The bridge subparser `metavar` is a hardcoded literal that was not updated when the `suggest-mapping` subparser was added, so the usage synopsis advertises a command set omitting the new verb while the auto-derived command listing includes it — an internal inconsistency and stale user-facing surface.
scenarios: A user runs `rebar bridge --help` and the usage line `{preview,run,...,projects} ...` omits suggest-mapping, contradicting the commands list below it
advisory.suggested_fix: Update metavar to `{preview,run,sync,status,pause,resume,fsck,check-access,setup,suggest-mapping,projects}` at bridge.py:43 and re-generate the byte-checked help/bridge.txt and cli-reference.md usage synopsis lines.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for _suggest_mapping_write error branches: unreadable/malformed existing rebar.toml, and an unwritable target, each asserting exit code 1 and the corresponding stderr message.
evidence: _suggest_mapping_write emits 'Error: cannot read existing config' + return 1 on `(OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError)`, 'Error: cannot serialize config' + return 1 on ConfigError, and 'Error: could not write config' + return 1 on OSError
search for 'cannot' and 'could not write' in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_probe.py returns (no matches)
only happy-path --write tests exist: test_probe_write_preserves_edits (line 285) and test_write_creates_new_rebar_toml_when_absent (line 594)
advisory.finding: The _suggest_mapping_write error branches are untested. The handler has three distinct failure paths each returning exit 1 with a specific stderr message — unreadable existing config (tomllib.TOMLDecodeError/OSError), serialization ConfigError, and OSError on atomic write — but no test exercises any of them; only the happy-path --write (preserve edits, create-when-absent) is covered.
scenarios: An existing rebar.toml with malformed TOML content is present when --write runs — the read-failure branch (exit 1, specific stderr) is never verified.
The target directory/file is unwritable — the OSError branch is never verified.

dropped.finding: The new nested TOML emitter's fail-closed-on-unsupported-scalar contract is untested: _config_writer._render_scalar was lifted to module scope specifically so _emit_nested_toml renders values 'identically' and raises ConfigError on an unsupported type, but the only fail-closed regression test (test_emit_toml_still_fail_closed_on_nesting) pins the OLD _emit_toml. No test drives _emit_nested_toml or _emit_config_toml with an unsupported value type (e.g. datetime/None), so a regression letting the nested path silently mis-emit would go undetected.
scenarios: A future change makes _emit_nested_toml swallow an unsupported type (e.g. emit repr of a datetime) — the round-trip tests use only str/int values, so this would not be caught.
